Upcoming Pause in Configuration Changes

Aug 10, 2026

As previously communicated, the Office of MaineCare Services is launching an upgraded MIHMS, our claims processing system, in October 2026. To support system readiness activities, MaineCare is temporarily pausing the implementation of configuration changes from the end of August to the end of October.

Coding and NDC Requests

Continue submitting coding requests to OMS.referencefile@maine.gov and NDC/J-Code Requests to MaineCareNDCrequest.DHHS@maine.gov. Requests submitted by August 19, 2026, if approved, will be implemented no later than the last synchronization on August 25, 2026. Continue to submit these requests as usual after these dates. MaineCare will review and document change requests beginning at the end of October.

Rate Change Requests

Continue submitting rate change requests as usual to MIHMSRateRqst.DHHS@maine.gov throughout this period. MaineCare will review and document change requests as appropriate for implementation beginning at the end of October.

Claims and Billing Inquiries

Continue directing claims and billing inquiries to Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. We will continue reviewing claim denials to determine if a configuration change is needed. MaineCare will review and document change requests as appropriate for implementation before the configuration pause or beginning at the end of October.

We appreciate your continued cooperation during this transition. If you have questions about the configuration pause or the status of a request, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.

Stakeholder Group Meeting: Nursing Facility Reform Transition Fund

Aug 10, 2026

Pursuant to Resolve 2025, Chapter 157 the Department of Health and Human Services is convening a group to examine the use of the Nursing Facility Reform Transition Fund, established under P.L. 2023, Chapter 643, Part SSS. The first meeting will be held on August 31, 2026 at 3:00 PM through Zoom. Meetings are open to the public. 

Register for the Zoom meeting. 

The group must submit a report to the Maine Legislature’s Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services no later than January 15, 2027, addressing the following: 

  • Nursing Facility Reform Transition Fund expenses to date;  

  • Plan for spending the remaining funds;  

  • Cycle for rebasing reimbursement rates; and  

  • Use of the fund to pay for cost-of-living increases for staff pay compared with the use of other funding sources for other cost-of-living increases for direct care services. 

For questions, please contact LTSS Initiatives Manager Amanda Nelson, or Deputy Director of Policy and Programs Olivia Alford.

Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) Clinical Eligibility Review and Billing Criteria for Section 45 and 46 Hospitals Update

Aug 10, 2026

Beginning September 1, 2026, IOP services delivered by hospitals enrolled under MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) Chapter II, Sections 45 and 46 will require clinical eligibility review and billing criteria in alignment with Medicare’s IOP services billing requirements.  

Effective for dates of service on, or after, September 1, 2026, hospitals delivering IOP services must: 

  1. Submit a clinical review request to Acentra Health before delivering services to determine a MaineCare member’s IOP service eligibility. Members determined to meet clinical eligibility criteria as defined in MBM, Chapter II, Section 65 will receive a Case ID number to authorize billing for the delivery of IOP services by Section 45 and 46 providers. 

  2. With clinical review approval, deliver IOP services in accordance with their hospital licensure and the requirements of MBM, Chapter II, Section 65.05-4.  

  3. Submit claims using the corresponding CPT/HCPCS codes or revenue codes for actual services delivered including modifier(s) as applicable. Condition Code 92 (CC 92) is required in Form Locator fields 18-24. 

  4. Retain the clinical review Case ID number in the member’s medical record. Because IOP services without a clinical review Case ID are not eligible for reimbursement, providers must maintain clinical review approval records for Program Integrity purposes. 

  5. Deliver services in accordance with Division of Licensing and Certification (DLC) requirements.   

Please note: This notice supersedes previous MaineCare Section 45 and 46 IOP billing instructions including, but not limited to, the June 14, 2023 and August 18, 2023 messages.  

Medicare’s claims criteria are outlined in the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) publication, including MLN 13496 – Billing Requirements for Intensive Outpatient Program Services with New Condition Code 92.

For questions regarding hospital licensure requirements for the delivery of IOP services, please reach out to Anna Blackwell, Associate Director of DLC: Medical Facilities Unit.  

For questions regarding IOP service and eligibility standards set forth in Section 65, or the billing requirements for providers enrolled under Sections 45 and 46, please contact Provider Relations Specialist Tiffany Norton.

entry.title: US Department of Labor finds urgent care employer failed to pay over $113K in owed wages to workers for required orientation, meetings, training — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
entry.content: ATLANTA – The U.S. Department of Labor has recovered $113,199 in back wages after an investigation found a Richmond Hill urgent care facility failed to pay its workers for hours worked and retaliated against a worker for questioning its pay practices.An investigation by the department’s Wage and Hour Division found that Premier Health Consultants LLC – operating as St. Joseph Candler Urgent Care – violated the Fair Labor Standards Act by paying straight time instead of time and one-half in overtime for all hours worked over 40 when employees were required to attend mandatory orientation, meetings, and training. The employer also required certain employees to work off the clock, resulting in unpaid overtime, and suspended a worker who questioned pay practices, all violations of the FLSA.Workers and employers can call the Wage and Hour Division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). Employers are encouraged to use the agency’s industry-specific compliance assistance toolkits to learn about their responsibilities under the laws enforced by the division. The agency’s PAID program offers employers an opportunity to self-report and resolve potential minimum wage and overtime violations under the FLSA, as well as certain potential violations under the Family and Medical Leave Act. Learn more about the Wage and Hour Division, including a search tool that workers can use if they think they may be owed back wages collected by the division. Download the agency’s free timesheet app for iOS and Android devices to track hours and pay.

2026 Maine Hire-A-Vet Campaign Kicks Off August 20!

You're invited! Are you looking for a new career? Maybe you are transitioning from military service, or just looking for a change?

Maine's annual Hire-A-Vet Campaign is a statewide effort with the goal of at least 100 employers hiring at least 100 veterans and military family members during a 100-day period.

The 2026 campaign kicks off Thursday, August 20, at the Augusta National Guard Armory and will be followed by monthly in-person hiring events throughout the state:

While the campaign is focused on veterans and their families, these events are open to ALL jobseekers!

The Maine Hire-A-Vet campaign provides support and resources to connect veterans with employers through a network of state and federal agencies, resources and nonprofits, education on military language and culture, recruiting and hiring assistance, and recognition for the hiring and advancement of veterans and military family members.

Title 5 License Maintenance Case

Aug 11, 2026

Providers whose license is under a Title 5 review may use your Title 5 notice to extend your enrollment with MaineCare in MIHMS by six months, and for every six months thereafter, until the Title 5 review is resolved. Providers must complete this update by submitting a maintenance case via the Health PAS Online Portal. They can use the Provider Maintenance User Guide for step-by-step instructions.

Select the “Title 5 License Extension” from the licensing board drop-down menu and complete the maintenance case as usual. Providers can use the ALMS website to search for your license and must take a screenshot to upload with the maintenance case to show the Title 5 status. 

Please ensure the "Term Date” is 6 months after the license expiration date. For example, if you submit your Title 5 review and your license ends on January 30, 2026, extend the “Term Date” out to July 30, 2026. As necessary, repeat this process every six months until the license is renewed. Once the license is renewed, submit another case with the new term date of the license. 

Providers take note of your license expiration dates and plan to submit a maintenance case to update that license information a minimum of 30 days prior to the license expiration date. Be sure to account for this when planning and submitting other maintenance cases.

Note: MaineCare will not reimburse providers for services rendered when they fail to renew and update your license within a maintenance case prior to its expiration.

For questions about this process, please contact Provider Enrollment at 1 (866) 690-5585 option 2.

The summary below outlines the timing requirements for initial and repeat Single Assessments, including the limited exceptions to the standard annual assessment cycle for children receiving medium- and high-intensity behavioral health services.

 

Situation

When is a Single Assessment Required?

Timing

Child already receiving services (no prior Single Assessment)

If the child has never had a Single Assessment, complete one before the next authorization is issued. After that, follow the standard annual reassessment schedule.

Before the next authorization (typically at the next Continued Stay Review (CSR)), then every 12 months

New request for medium- or high-intensity services

Complete a Single Assessment before submitting the initial referral or authorization request.

Initial assessment

Child continues receiving medium- or high-intensity services

Repeat the Single Assessment to confirm ongoing eligibility. Continue submitting CSRs between annual assessments.

Every 12 months

Child residing in a Children’s Residential Care Facility (CRCF)

Complete a Single Assessment when discharge planning begins to determine eligibility for community-based services after discharge.

At discharge planning

On a CRCF wait list

Every 6 months

If no Single Assessment has been completed and the current authorization is nearing expiration, complete an initial Single Assessment before the next authorization. After that, follow the annual reassessment schedule.

At the first CSR after Single Assessment implementation, then every 12 months thereafter.

entry.title: USDA Distributes Oral Rabies Vaccine for Wildlife in Northern Maine — Maine Department of Health and Human Services News
entry.content:
Aug 11, 2026

In cooperation with the Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC), officials from U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Wildlife Services will distribute oral rabies vaccine (ORV) baits this week. USDA Wildlife Services will distribute nearly 599,000 ORV baits in Aroostook County from August 12 through August 24.

The fall ORV bait distribution follows this past spring’s distribution and is in response to continued rabid raccoon detections in Aroostook County. The USDA’s Wildlife Services spreads ORV baits to reduce the spread of the raccoon rabies virus in Maine. The baits help limit the potential for human and domestic animal exposures to the rabies virus through contact with infected wild animals.

Crews will spread the bait by air in rural areas and by vehicle in more populated areas. Each bait is a fishmeal-coated cube or sachet about one to two inches in size. Although humans and pets cannot get rabies from contact with the bait, they should not touch or move them.

Studies show that ORV baits are safe in many species of animals, including domestic dogs and cats. While dogs may get upset stomachs if they eat a lot of bait, there are no known long-term health risks. If a person has skin contact with a bait cube or sachet, rinse the affected area with warm water and soap. For concerns about a person or pet touching or eating a bait, call the Maine CDC’s 24-hour line at 800-821-5821.

Since 2003, the USDA’s Wildlife Services has worked to halt the spread of raccoon rabies in northern Maine. They also collaborate with Canadian officials in New Brunswick and Quebec to reduce the presence of rabies across Maine and Canada. The ORV bait distribution program in Maine is part of a larger effort by the USDA’s Wildlife Services to prevent the westward spread of raccoon rabies. This effort creates a barrier along the Appalachian Mountains from the Canadian border to Alabama.

Rabies is a virus that infects the nervous system of humans and other mammals. It spreads mainly through a bite from an infected animal. Once symptoms develop, rabies is almost always fatal. Timely post-exposure treatment can prevent disease in people. Approximately 90 percent of reported animal rabies cases in the U.S. occur in wildlife. As of August 10, 2026, 28 animals tested positive for rabies this year in 12 counties across Maine. These animals include raccoons, skunks, foxes, bats, and a goat.

To help protect yourself and your pet against rabies:

  • Keep your pets and livestock up to date on rabies vaccinations.
  • Feed pets indoors.
  • Keep garbage cans or other sources of food tightly secured.
  • Do not feed, touch, or adopt wild animals. Be cautious of stray dogs and cats.
  • Do not move wildlife. This can spread rabies into new areas.
  • Wash bite or scratch wounds with soap and water for 10 to 15 minutes.

Who to contact:

  • If an animal bites or scratches you, contact a health care provider.
  • If an animal bites or scratches your pet, contact your veterinarian.
  • To report a dead or suspicious-acting animal in northern Maine, contact the USDA’s Wildlife Services. In other parts of Maine, contact the nearest Maine Regional Communications Dispatch Center.

For more information:

  • USDA Rabies webpage
  • Maine CDC Rabies webpage
  • USDA Wildlife Services: 1-866-487-3297
  • Maine CDC disease reporting & consultation line: 1-800-821-5821 (available 24/7)

Photo of bait types: The bottom two bait types in the photo are a fishmeal-coated sachet(bottom) and cube(middle) and are the only two used in this ORV bait drop in Maine.

entry.title: Maine CDC: Childhood Vaccine Guidance Remains Unchanged Following Federal Action — Maine Department of Health and Human Services News
entry.content:
Aug 11, 2026

Maine will continue to follow the guidance of the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) on childhood vaccine recommendations, despite President Donald Trump’s executive order on childhood vaccinations, per the Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC).

“President Trump and Secretary Kennedy are playing politics with the lives of our nation’s children. Vaccines are safe and effective and save lives,” said Governor Janet Mills. “Maine will continue to follow the science and the facts, and our approach to vaccines remains unchanged by yesterday’s executive order.” 

“Vaccines are our most effective defense against vaccine-preventable illnesses,” said Dr. Puthiery Va, Director of the Maine CDC.“In Maine, vaccines remain available at no cost to eligible children through the Maine CDC’s Immunization Program. Maine’s school and child care immunization requirements remain unchanged by federal actions to date.”

As the AAP has noted in their 8/10 statement in response to this executive order:

 “Vaccine recommendations from the American Academy of Pediatrics are tailored to the health of children living in the United States and are based on decades of research and systematic tracking of real-world experiences. Pediatricians recommend children receive certain vaccines at specific ages based on when children's immune systems will respond best and when they are most vulnerable to certain diseases. Sometimes this means children will receive a single shot that protects against multiple diseases, or they may receive multiple vaccines at one visit.” 

Beginning in 2021, Maine removed non-medical exemptions from the school and child care immunization requirements pursuant Public Law 2019, Ch. 154. That decision was upheld by a vote of 72.81 percent of Maine voters at the ballot box in 2020.

entry.content: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to grant a Clean Air Act (CAA or Act) petition submitted by the state of New Hampshire on December 24, 2025. The petition requests that the EPA remove the State of New Hampshire from the Ozone Transport Region (OTR) based on New Hampshire's continued attainment of the ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) and technical analyses demonstrating that the additional control of emissions from the state will not significantly contribute to ozone attainment in any area in the OTR. The OTR was established by the 1990 Clean Air Act Amendments and included the States of Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Vermont, the District of Columbia, and portions of northern Virginia.

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Aug 12, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training starting September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal.

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition.

Steps you need to take to attend training

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities.
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions.
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance.
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference.

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions

Course Name

Description

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users.

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality.

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities.

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC)

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources.

 

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility.

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login.
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account.
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window.
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address.
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript.
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile.
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods:
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email.
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event.
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink.

Do not forward meeting invitations to other attendees. Each participant must register through the LMS to receive course access, training credit, and post-training evaluation access.

We are offering optional virtual support sessions during the week of August 17, 2026 to help with LMS access and training registration and to ask questions about upcoming training topics. Pharmacy Prior Authorization and Claims Denials: Enroll to Avoid Denials

Aug 13, 2026

As previously communicated, billing providers must include the National Provider Identifier (NPI) of an enrolled MaineCare practitioner who is ordering, prescribing, or referring on claims submitted to MaineCare. This is a federal requirement. In the next few months, MaineCare will begin to deny pharmacy PAs for prescriptions written by providers who are not enrolled with MaineCare, and will subsequently begin to deny Point of Sale pharmacy claims that do not have the NPI of an enrolled prescriber on the claim.

This requirement is for:

  • All prescription claims, including Point of Sale claims
  • Clinical laboratories for ordered tests
  • Imaging centers for ordered imaging procedures
  • Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics and Supplies (DMEPOS)

  

Enroll with MaineCare today! 

Make sure your patients can continue to get their medications covered by ensuring any unenrolled prescribing providers complete an online application through the Health PAS Online Portal. Providers that do not plan to seek MaineCare reimbursement may continue prescribing medications to MaineCare members by enrolling specifically as a Non-Billing, Ordering, Prescribing or Referring (NOPR) provider, which is a shorter process. The NOPR enrollment is faster and requires less documentation than a regular MaineCare enrollment – and is free to complete.

We encourage unenrolled prescribers to start by visiting the Provider Enrollment & Revalidation webpage for helpful resources to guide you through the enrollment process.

Contact us for assistance. 

For assistance with the enrollment process, please contact Provider Services by email or call 1-866-690-5585, Option 2. TTY users dial 711.

Title IV Postsecondary Institutions: Workforce Pell Program Application Now Open

MAINE- The State Workforce Development Board (SWDB) - https://www.maine.gov/swb/board/index.shtml announced the launch of Maine's Workforce Pell Application - https://www.worksourcemaine.com/pages/workforce-pell , providing eligible Title IV postsecondary institutions with an online process to seek approval to offer Workforce Pell-eligible programs.

The launch of the application follows the U.S. Department of Education's publication of the final Workforce Pell regulations - https://www.ed.gov/about/news/press-release/us-department-of-education-issues-final-rule-create-new-workforce-pell-grant-program (effective July 20, 2026). Workforce Pell expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term workforce training programs that prepare students for high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand careers. Under Workforce Pell, states are responsible for reviewing and certifying eligible programs before approval by the U.S. Department of Education.

"Workforce Pell opens the door to new education and career opportunities for more people across our state," said Vaughan Woodruff, Chair, State Workforce Development Board. "The Maine Workforce Pell program makes it easier for individuals to access those opportunities, strengthening the futures of Maine workers and Maine's businesses."

On July 30, the SWDB approved the Maine Workforce Pell Program Determination Policy - https://www.worksourcemaine.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/final-workforce-pell-determination-policy-8.11.2026.pdf , establishing the state's process for identifying, reviewing, and recommending eligible short-term workforce training programs for Workforce Pell. Developed in partnership with the Maine Department of Labor, Maine Department of Education, Finance Authority of Maine, Maine Community College System, and University of Maine System, the policy is designed to align eligible programs with high-skill, high-wage, in-demand occupations; ensure quality outcomes for students; and provide a transparent and consistent process for institutions and learners.

"Workforce Pell is an important step toward building a stronger workforce and expanding opportunities for people to gain the skills they need to succeed," said Laura Fortman, Commissioner of the Maine Department of Labor. Save-the-Date: DHHS Partner Briefing on Federal Medicaid Work Requirements and Increased Renewals

Aug 14, 2026

DHHS Partner Briefing on Federal Medicaid Work Requirements and Increased Renewals 

When: Monday, August 24, 2026, 3:00 – 4:30 PM 

Where: Virtual, please register in advance. 

You are invited to join a Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) briefing to learn about plans to implement federal changes to Medicaid (in Maine, MaineCare) eligibility that will go into effect on January 1, 2027.   

During this webinar, the DHHS Office for Family Independence (OFI) and Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) will provide an overview of upcoming changes to MaineCare eligibility for Expansion Adults: 

  • New Work Requirements;  

  • Coverage renewals every 6 months instead of every 12 months; and 

  • Retroactive coverage of 1 month instead of 3 months. 

MaineCare Expansion members are adults between 19 and 64 years old who get MaineCare based on their income. They do not meet the Social Security disability guidelines or have Medicare. OFI and OMS will also provide an update on planning for implementation and communications.   

We are also pleased to share the Partner Communications Toolkit, which can be found at MaineCare.gov/work. This toolkit includes materials you can download and print or include in your digital and social media channels to reach the populations in your community that will need to know more and take action to meet the new federal Work Requirements for Medicaid.  

Important Timelines to Note:  

  • August 14, 2026: Launch of Federal Changes and Work Requirements webpages, and Partner Toolkit launch – first phase  

  • August 24, 2026: Partner briefing focused on what to know 

  • Beginning August 19, 2026: OFI will send knowledge building letters and text messages to MaineCare Expansion Adults 

  • Fall 2026: Continued communication and partnership with providers and community partners.  

  • Late 2026 and through 2027: OFI will provide direct 1:1 phone call outreach to impacted MaineCare Expansion Adults ahead of their renewal month. 

  • January 2027 and forward: MaineCare Expansion Adults will need to meet Work Requirements starting with their first renewal in 2027 and will have 6-month renewals from that point on. 

Register and join to learn more and assist with sharing information and resources in your community.     

After registering, you will receive a confirmation email containing information about joining the meeting. Feel free to share this invitation with other interested organizations who may wish to attend.   

Space is limited, so please register early.

entry.title: The CFPB to Cease Discretionary Publication of Complaint Narratives and Visualizations — Consumer Financial Protection Bureau — Newsroom
entry.content:
Washington, D.C. – Today, the CFPB is ceasing publication of unverified complaint narratives and visualizations.  As the CFPB has long acknowledged, the publication in the Consumer Complaint Database of unverified complaint narratives and associated data visualizations is entirely discretionary. Many years of experience have demonstrated that the utility of such publication is minimal, while often causing confusion and providing misleading data.  By their very nature, complaint narratives reflect negative consumer experiences and present only one side of an issue. Additionally, these unverified allegations do not always describe violations of the law and the complaint process does not verify the allegations in each consumer’s complaint narrative, nor can it, as a practical matter. Publishing such narratives in the Database provides a less-than-representative sample of one-sided experiences that cannot provide consumers with a balanced and accurate view of companies’ compliance with their legal obligations.

Publishing narratives and visualizations given these deficiencies risks confusing and misleading consumers, who should otherwise be able to rely on the Bureau for authoritative information as they choose the products and services that meet their individual needs. It also needlessly harms companies’ reputations.

To more closely align the Bureau’s operations with its statutory authorities and to mitigate the risk to consumers and companies of publishing confusing or misleading information, the CFPB will cease its discretionary publication of consumers’ complaint narratives and visualizations in the Database. The Bureau considers previously published narratives to be in the public domain for Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) purposes. Like the Federal Trade Commission, the Bureau is placing these narratives and is proactively disclosing them in the CFPB’s FOIA Reading Room.

The CFPB remains committed to meeting its statutory obligations and will continue to collect, monitor, and respond to consumers’ complaints, to systematically review and assess how well companies are providing complete, accurate, and timely responses, to share consumer complaint information securely with prudential regulators, FTC, other federal and state agencies, and to disclose certain data in response to FOIA requests.

About us

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau is a 21st century agency that implements and enforces Federal consumer financial law and ensures that markets for consumer financial products are fair, transparent, and competitive.

entry.title: Continuing the Fight Against the Opioid Epidemic — Governor of Maine — Newsroom Press Releases
entry.content:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

Over the five years leading up to 2019, more than 1,600 people in Maine died from drug overdoses. We were losing a person every day. About 8% of all babies in Maine were born substance-exposed—that's three each day. The life-saving drug Naloxone was not generally available. There were few treatment beds, and when someone was ready to get into recovery, even fewer treatment options were available if they didn't have health insurance.

When I took office, I knew that what Maine had been doing for so many years just wasn't working. We needed a coordinated response that broke down the silos of government, set aside the stigma, and spoke out about every aspect of the opioid epidemic. I promised that we would put the full force of my Administration behind the families who lost loved ones, the businesses who lost employees, and all the communities that have been diminished by this public health crisis. 

So my first executive order, signed on my first day in office, fulfilled the will of the people of Maine and expanded MaineCare to more than 90,000 people. Today, nearly 40,000 people receive treatment for substance use disorder through MaineCare. Expanding health insurance was a critical first step to confronting the opioid crisis.

I named Gordon Smith as my Director of Opioid Response, and I signed the second executive order with basic strategies and specific action steps. That order established a Prevention and Recovery Cabinet made up of commissioners from 14 government agencies and the Attorney General's Office and the Judicial Branch.

We outlined key steps to preventing overdoses and deaths, including making Naloxone widely available statewide, and since early 2019, we've distributed more than 870,000 doses of Naloxone, which has saved thousands of lives.

We then outlined steps to expand effective treatment and recovery measures, including training 250 recovery coaches and funding recovery coaches in ten emergency departments. Now we've trained more than 4,000 individuals as recovery coaches, and we've increased the number of certified recovery residences from 11 to 119.

We've created youth recovery coaching programs in Hancock and Washington counties in the schools, creating peer-to-peer connections that can give a young person the hope to face the future. And we held statewide trainings and leadership conferences, which taught more than 400 youth how to create positive change in their communities. 

We created TreatmentConnection.com, a one-stop-shop for individuals seeking treatment that allows them to find out in real time what there is available for behavioral health services among more than 500 providers. Since that went live in 2025, TreatmentConnection has been used 8,000 times.

We're also increasing good-paying jobs for people in recovery, rewarding businesses who understand the unique experiences of people in recovery. And we've created the Recovery Friendly Workplaces designation, a certification held by 86 businesses who employ nearly 25,000 people statewide.

You know, we're not giving up on interdiction as well, making sure we take drugs off the street as much as possible to keep people from becoming addicted in the first place. My Administration is doing what we can in a responsible manner to stop deadly drugs from reaching Maine, to prevent substance abuse in the first place, to treat it when we can't prevent it, to set people on a lifelong path to recovery, and, above all else, to save lives.

From January to June of this year, fatal overdoses decreased by nearly 9% in Maine. This is the fourth consecutive year of declining overdose deaths. And that's welcome news, but we know we can't be complacent. Every overdose is a tragic and, I believe, preventable loss of a valued life. So let's all recommit to supporting people as they start, stumble, or resume their recovery, and to responding to new phases of the opioid epidemic to save lives.

This is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

Natural Resources Disaster Relief Assistance Program (NRDRAP) applications Open today, Friday, August 14

August 14, 2026

The Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF) is opening applications for the Natural Resources Disaster Relief Assistance Program (NRDRAP) today, Friday, August 14, 2026.

Maine farmers, forestry businesses, aquaculture producers, and other eligible producers who experienced weather-related losses in 2023 or 2024 may qualify for financial assistance.

Eligible losses may include crop loss, aquaculture loss, standing timber loss, harvested timber loss, on-farm and forestry infrastructure loss, and bare-ground practices necessary to mitigate land loss.

Application period: August 14, 2026, through November 6, 2026.

Applications will be accepted through the online portal. Paper applications are available upon request.

Producers can prepare now. Applicants are encouraged to begin gathering documentation, including:

  • Ownership or lease documentation
  • Parcel ID information
  • FSA Farm Number, if applicable
  • Tax or business identification information
  • Photos or records documenting damage

Other records related to weather-related losses in 2023 and/or 2024 DACF will provide technical assistance throughout the application period. Virtual office hours will be held every Friday from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. beginning August 14.

For updates, eligibility information, and application details, visit maine.gov/dacf/nrdrap, email NRDRA.DACF@maine.gov, or call (207) 530-3144.

Reminder for Billing Attending Provider on UB-04 and 837I Claims, CR 110840

Aug 17, 2026

This is a reminder that the attending provider is required on all UB-04 and 837I claims. MaineCare denies UB-04 and 837I claims submitted without an enrolled attending provider.

The attending provider is the individual who has overall responsibility for the patient’s medical care and treatment reported in the claim/encounter. The attending provider requirement includes all claim submission methods (paper, HealthPAS Online Portal, or 837I).

MaineCare continues to monitor claims for compliance with applicable billing requirements and to work collaboratively with individual providers and provider associations to address identified issues and provide guidance where needed. While progress has been made over the last several months, a higher-than-expected volume of billing errors continue to be identified specific to the attending provider requirements. MaineCare remains committed to supporting providers in improving claim accuracy and compliance with program requirements.

To help you make corrections to your claims, below are the most common errors we see:

  1. There is no information in the attending provider field, or the information is not valid.
  2. Providers are submitting a Type 2 NPI instead of a Type 1 NPI. Providers must use a Type 1 NPI unless self-referred screening mammography is the only service billed on the claim.
  3. The attending provider is not enrolled in MaineCare or the provider is not enrolled in MaineCare for the date of service on the claim.

Please see the March 23, 2023 message for more information or call Provider Services with questions at 1-866-690-5585.

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Aug 17, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training starting September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live.

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition.

Steps you need to take to attend training

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities.
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions.
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance.
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference.

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions

Course Name

Description

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users.

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.

Attention Trading Partners: Take Action Now Before MaineCare’s New Online Portal Goes Live

Aug 17, 2026

A refreshed and upgraded MIHMS is coming in mid October 2026. The Office of MaineCare Services (OMS), in partnership with Gainwell Technologies, is launching an upgraded MIHMS, to bring enhanced security, improved usability, and a more modern experience to better support your day-to-day work.

The upgrade will include a new “MaineCare Partner Portal” that will replace what is known today as the “Health PAS Online Portal.” Please note that, until the October go-live, we will continue using the name “Health PAS Online Portal” in communications related to current functionality.

You can read more about the benefits to providers and members on the Health PAS Online Portal.

Trading Partners Preparation

This message is part of a series about changes to how trading partners will access the new portal and what you must do now to prepare for these changes.

Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live.

Portal Access Impacts and Required Actions Before Go‑Live

The preparation activities and changes below will improve system security by ensuring the right people have the right access, at go-live and ongoing. Most actions are only for Admin (R7) users.

Most important: Providers with duplicate emails need to make changes to their portal user accounts now to assist with account migration to the upgraded portal. On September 1, we will terminate current Admin (R7) user accounts that share an email address with another user account. We will not terminate Admin (R7) user accounts if they are the only Admin (R7) on the Trading Partner account.

If a user account is terminated and they still need portal access, another user with Admin Rights (R7) can invite the terminated user using a unique email address, not the one previously used.

Activity/Change

Your Action

Why it Matters

What’s Next?

At go-live, MaineCare will only migrate Admin (R7) accounts to the new portal.

 

MaineCare will not migrate inactive accounts.

Designate at least one active Admin (R7) per organization, and two for backup coverage.

 

Trading Partners with large user populations should plan for sufficient Admin (R7) coverage to avoid access delays after go-live; we recommend one Admin (R7) per 25 users.

 

Remove inactive Admin (R7) accounts.

After go-live, Admin (R7) users will need to re-invite all other active users. More Admin (R7) users mean less re-invitation work for each user.

 

Trading Partners have an existing and ongoing responsibility to remove inactive users to help keep our systems and data secure.

 

We will monitor the number and activity of Admin (R7) users per Trading Partner and will reach out to individual Trading Partners if needed.

In the new portal, your username will be your email address.

MaineCare will not migrate accounts that share an email address.

Confirm that each active Admin (R7) user account has its own unique email address.

OMS will deactivate accounts that continue to share email addresses as we approach go-live.

After go-live, Admin (R7) users will need immediate access to the portal to invite other users and avoid disruption in Trading Partner work.

We will monitor accounts that share email addresses and will reach out to individual Trading Partners if needed.

Admin (R7) users will invite other users to the portal and designate your roles after go-live.

 

Admin (R7) will be able to choose from ~40 permissions, compared to 9 today.

Prepare to invite users after go-live:

  • Know who needs a user account in the new portal
  • Know the permission level each user will need to have

 

Admin (R7) users will need to invite other users shortly after go-live to avoid a disruption in Trading Partner work.

 

We will share more information during trainings including role definitions, templates, and other guidance.

 

For questions, please email Provider Services or call 1-866-690-5585.

entry.title: Statement of Attorney General Aaron M. Frey Prompted by the Shadow Hearing on the Use of Deadly Force by ICE in the death of Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero — Maine Attorney General Press Releases
entry.content:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Contact: Danna Hayes, Danna.hayes@maine.gov

Statement of Attorney General Aaron M. Frey Prompted by the Shadow Hearing on the Use of Deadly Force by ICE in the death of Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero

AUGUSTA – The Office of the Maine Attorney General continues to actively investigate the shooting death of Mr. Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero by a federal Enforcement Removal Operations Officer in Biddeford on July 13, 2026.

Under Maine Law, the Attorney General’s Office has exclusive responsibility both for any criminal investigation of a homicide and for the use of deadly force by law enforcement acting in an official capacity. In cooperation with relevant local, state and federal agencies, this office has been collecting, processing, and analyzing evidence to determine whether Maine law authorizes legal action to address the conduct.

Once the investigation is complete and the Attorney General has determined whether available evidence supports any action under Maine law, the entire file will be provided to the Maine Deadly Force Review Panel, as contemplated by 5 M.R.S § 200-K, for review and recommendations in effort to minimize and, to the greatest extent possible, prevent the use of deadly force. 

As a general matter, neither the Office of the Maine Attorney General nor the Maine Deadly Force Review Panel may exercise jurisdiction over the practices of the Department of Homeland Security, and it will be the responsibility of either the federal administration or Congress to address any questions raised by such review.

Finally, the Office of the Maine Attorney General is keenly aware of the public interest in this case and is committed to a thorough, impartial investigation that ensures meaningful transparency and public confidence. While completeness and transparency are objectives of equal importance, protecting the integrity of the investigation takes priority while evidence is still being gathered. This Office is regularly assessing whether substantive updates may be made available without interfering with this important work. At the appropriate time, more information will be made publicly available. In the meantime, we appreciate patience as we proceed.

The mussel seed would be harvested using specially designed machiner y that is lowered over the collecti on netting to remove the seed with a brushing mechanism. The harvesting machine uses a hydraulic system to then pump the seed into a seventy -four-foot transport vessel. [¶3] Acadia intends to use the harvesting machine seasonally, from May to October, for up to a total of three weeks during those months. W hen not in use, the machine would be stored on a twenty-foot-by-twenty-foot floating raft permanently moored within the lease sit e. Dear Employer,

Workplace safety and labor law requirements can seem complex - join the Maine Department of Labor for no-cost upcoming trainings! Please forward to your Safety Coordinators/Managers.

Upcoming classes:

Life Safety Code 101- September 1, 2026 I 8:30 a.m. 4:30 p.m. SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Department of Labor, 45 Commerce Drive, Augusta

This one-day class will provide a working overview of National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) Standard 101 "Life Safety Code" for fire and life safety in the building environment. Topics covered will include classification of occupancy types, adequate means of egress, occupant load factors, and occupancy specific hazards to fire and life safety. This class addresses commonly asked labor-related questions.

Respiratory Protection September 10, 2026 I 8:30 a.m. 4:00 p.m. SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Department of Labor, 45 Commerce Drive, Augusta

Where workers are required to wear respirators to do their jobs, employers need a respiratory protection program. This course helps you determine your respiratory protection needs and covers all the elements of a written respiratory protection program.

Notice of Agency Rule-making Proposal

 

AGENCY: Department of Health and Human Services, MaineCare Services, Division of Policy

CHAPTER NUMBER AND RULE TITLE: 10-144 C.M.R. Ch. 101, MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) [Ch. I, Sec. 1, General Administrative Policies and Procedures]

TYPE OF RULE: Routine Technical

PROPOSAL FILING NUMBER: 2026-P195

BRIEF SUMMARY: This rulemaking is proposed via two, simultaneous private citizen petitions submitted to the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) on June 23, 2026, to adopt or modify a rule. The petitioners provided the specific rule changes proposed here as part of their petitions. Under 5 M.R.S. § 8055, the Department of Health and Human Services (Department) is required to initiate rulemaking proceedings on the petitioners’ proposals within 60 days because each petition was signed by 150 or more registered voters. Because the Department may only propose one set of amendments to a rule at any given time, this rulemaking combines the two petitioned rule amendments into a single rulemaking.

The proposed rule would amend Chapter I, Section 1 of the MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) to require the Department to conduct in-person, On-Site Reviews and On-Site Inspections of MaineCare provider business or service locations and authorize the Department to impose sanctions when a provider fails to permit access to the Department for such On-Site Visit, Review, or Inspection. The proposed rule would require the Department to suspend a MaineCare provider’s claims payments, under defined criteria, and to escrow withheld payments upon notice of improper payment with the issuance of a Payment Suspension and Escrow Order (PSEO). The rule proposes to escrow such suspended and hold payments until a final determination is made as to the existence and amount of any improper payment. The petitioners also propose that the Department require providers under payment suspension to continue to deliver medically necessary covered services to current MaineCare members.

The petitioners also propose that the Department work with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to obtain any necessary approvals to amend the State Plan to enact these reforms.

entry.title: US Department of Labor announces successful resolution of rapid response labor mechanism matter at Grupo Yazaki S.A. de C.V. — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
entry.content: WASHINGTON – The United States today announced the successful resolution of the USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism matter at the Grupo Yazaki, S.A. de C.V. facility located in Leon, Guanajuato, Mexico. The United States has resumed liquidation of tariffs on goods from the Yazaki facility, which manufactures automotive components, wire harnesses, and electronic components. The resolution represents real progress in protecting American workers’ ability to compete in trade, requiring Mexican manufacturers to comply with Mexican law and the provisions of the USMCA. It is another win for the Trump Administration, whose America First approach puts American workers first by ensuring auto parts suppliers in other countries do not undermine worker protections to gain an unfair trade advantage or attract investment. The Department of Labor’s Bureau of International Labor Affairs and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative facilitated a resolution with the Government of Mexico to remediate workers’ claims at Yazaki.Actions taken by Yazaki to address the matter include:Issuing a neutrality statement and company guidelines related to freedom of association and collective bargaining;Adopting a policy to respect the rights of minority unions that do not hold ownership of the collective bargaining agreement; andSigning a letter of commitment to deliver the neutrality statement and company guidelines to workers, train workers on the same, provide space for Mexico’s Secretariat of Labor and Social Welfare to train workers on freedom of association and collective bargaining, and publish and disseminate to workers the company’s minority union policy.Actions taken by Mexico to address the matter include: Delivering in-person trainings for all company personnel on freedom of association and collective bargaining; andMonitoring the facility and engaging with the workers and the company throughout its review period.Based on these measures, the United States Trade Representative directed the Secretary of the Treasury to resume liquidation of unliquidated entries of goods from the facility. Background The United States‑Mexico‑Canada Agreement’s innovative enforcement tool, the Rapid Response Labor Mechanism, enables the U.S. government to act quickly and directly at the facility level when workers in Mexico are denied the rights of freedom of association and collective bargaining. The United States Trade Representative and the Secretary of Labor co-chair the Interagency Labor Committee for Monitoring and Enforcement that coordinates U.S. efforts related to enforcement actions on USMCA labor obligations, including the RRM. On October 20, 2025, the ILC received an RRM petition from Sindicato Independiente Nacional de Trabajadores y Trabajadoras de la Industria Automotriz, a Mexican independent union. The petition alleges that Yazaki and an incumbent union at the facility have violated workers’ rights by interfering in employees’ union activity and retaliating against workers because of their attempts to organize an independent union at the facility. The ILC reviews RRM petitions that it receives, and the accompanying information, within 30 days. The ILC determined that there was sufficient, credible evidence of a denial of rights enabling the good faith invocation of enforcement mechanisms. As a result, on November 19, 2025, the United States Trade Representative submitted a request to Mexico to review the matter. Mexico accepted the request, conducted an investigation, and worked with Yazaki to implement measures aimed at safeguarding freedom of association and collective bargaining rights. The United States has reviewed the matter and concluded the situation to have been remediated.As a result of the above actions taken by Yazaki and Mexico to resolve the action, the United States agrees that there is no ongoing denial of rights. Ambassador Greer’s letter directing the Secretary of the Treasury to resume liquidation of unliquidated entries of goods from the facility is available here. Learn more about the department’s work to make global competition fair for American workers.

Upcoming Federal Changes to MaineCare Eligibility for Some Non-citizens

Aug 20, 2026

We are writing to inform you about an upcoming change to MaineCare eligibility that may affect some of your MaineCare patients. This change is required by federal legislation signed into law in July 2025 (also called H.R.1, One Big Beautiful Bill, P.L.119-21, or Working Families Tax Cuts Act) that made changes to the Medicaid program nationally. These changes apply in all states, including Maine.

Beginning October 1, 2026, MaineCare eligibility is changing for some noncitizen groups. As a result, some individuals who currently receive full MaineCare benefits will no longer qualify for full coverage and will instead be eligible only for Emergency Services MaineCare. An explanation of covered benefits under Emergency Services MaineCare is available in the MaineCare Benefits Manual, Chapter 1, Section 1.02-4(D).

These changes will not affect children under age 21, or pregnant individuals through 12 months after the end of their pregnancy. Please note that the Office for Family Independence (OFI) is still completing the state rulemaking process to implement these federal requirements.

What You Should Know:

  • The eligibility changes are expected to take effect on October 1, 2026.
  • Members who are affected will receive a formal Notice of Decision from OFI before any eligibility changes take place. These notices are expected to be mailed in September 2026.
  • Some members received an early awareness letter in June or July 2026 to let them know they may be affected. This letter was informational only and is not an eligibility determination.

How You Can Help:

As a trusted healthcare provider, you can play an important role in helping your patients prepare for these changes by:

  • Encouraging patients to read any letters they receive from MaineCare or OFI.
  • Reminding patients to report any changes to their immigration status to OFI if it has changed since May 2026, as this could affect their eligibility.
  • Encouraging patients to continue using their MaineCare benefits to access covered healthcare services, including getting checkups and preventive care and refilling prescriptions, while they remain eligible.
  • Helping reassure patients that an early awareness letter does not mean their coverage has already changed.

Resources:

We developed resources to help providers understand these federal changes and answer patient questions. You can find these resources in this linked toolkit.

MaineCare and OFI will continue to share updates through provider e-messages and our webpage and other typical communication channels as additional information becomes available.

See the Non-citizen Resource Guide for resources that you can share with your patients to help support them in preparing for this change, and after their full MaineCare coverage ends. This list will be continually updated as we become aware of new resources.

If you have additional resources for us to add, please email MaineCare at Communications.MaineCare@maine.gov

If members have questions about covered services, please have them call Member Services at 1-800-977-6740.

Thank you for your continued partnership and for helping to ensure MaineCare members receive accurate information and access to the care they need.

entry.content: JANESVILLE, WI – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a Wisconsin-based food products manufacturer after two incidents involving industrial kettles releasing hot steam and liquid, causing three worker deaths and two serious injuries.Investigators with the department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration responded to the first incident on Feb. 12, 2026, at IPMF LLC, operating as NaturPak. The incident involved the lid of an industrial kettle unexpectedly opening after a clogged vent line led to pressure building up, and then releasing steam, liquid, and organic material onto two employees nearby. One of the employees was also struck by an object and suffered a concussion. Both employees were hospitalized, and one later passed away because of complications from their injuries. A month later, OSHA investigators responded to another incident involving multiple worker hospitalizations on March 18, when a kettle lid opened while under pressure releasing steam, hot liquid, and organic material, burning three workers. Two workers were fatally injured and another hospitalized. OSHA issued the employer one serious citation for the design and usage of kettles leading to pressure and thermal burn hazards; a repeat citation for exposing workers to falls to lower levels; and an other-than-serious citation for failing to notify employees working adjacent to permit-required confined spaces.OSHA also issued serious citations for exposing workers to thermal hazards without quick access to emergency water. The employer also received citations for exposing workers to falls into the kettles and for failure to assess personal protective equipment for thermal risks. In addition, OSHA issued repeat citations for failure to develop, document, and utilize lockout/tagout procedures for the kettles and failure to train employees on lockout/tagout procedures. The agency issued citations with $115,850 in penalties related to the inspection opened on Feb. 12 and $248,250 in penalties for the inspection opened on March 18. IPMF LLC has 15 business days from receipt of its citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.

Attention Trading Partners: MIHMS Upgrade October Payment Cycle Changes and System Access Limitations

Aug 21, 2026

As previously communicated, the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) is preparing to launch an upgraded version of MIHMS, MaineCare’s claims processing system. The upgrade is currently scheduled to go live on October 10, 2026. To support a smooth transition, OMS must implement temporary system access limitations and adjustments to payment cycles in October.

From Friday, October 2 at 8:00 PM until Monday, October 12 at 8:00 AM, MIHMS will be in a “data freeze” while OMS completes final system readiness and transition activities.

Changes to October payment cycles:

Review this information and plan billing accordingly to prepare for the transition.

Payment Cycle Date Payment Impact Claim Submission Deadline for Inclusion in Payment Cycle*
Wednesday, 9/30/26 Last regular payment before the data freeze Friday, 9/25/26, 5:00 AM
Thursday, 10/1/26 Extra payment before the data freeze Wednesday, 9/30/26, 5:00 AM
There will be no payment on Wednesday, October 7.
Thursday, 10/15/26 First payment after data freeze, in upgraded system

Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) submission: Continuous through data freeze up to Tuesday, 10/13/26, 2:00 PM

Portal submission:

Before data freeze: Friday, 10/2/26, 7:59 PM

After data freeze: Tuesday, 10/13/26, 2:00 PM
Wednesday, 10/21/26 Regular payment, in upgraded system Friday, 10/16/26, 5:00 AM

*As always, timely submission does not guarantee that the claim will process in time for the next payment cycle. OMS may take up to 30 days to process and pay a claim, depending on any edits or issues that may cause the claim to pend for manual review, as well as other processing requirements that may require the full 30-day timeframe.

Non-claims payments:

By September 1, OMS will communicate with any providers expecting non-claims payments that may be affected by the schedule described above.

Preparing for the changes to October payment cycles:

Beginning September 1, 2026 7:00 AM, OMS will return the HealthPAS Online Portal to its previous regular operating hours. Providers will again have 24/7 access to the portal, for additional flexibility and time to submit claims outside of standard business hours. 

We strongly encourage providers to submit claims approaching timely filing limits in the next few weeks to avoid potential submission delays. The planned data freeze does not modify existing Medicaid timely filing requirements. Providers remain responsible for ensuring claims are submitted within the established timely filing guidelines.

Other system access limitations:

Providers can find other expected impacts of the data freeze in this FAQ. Topics include:

  • HealthPAS Online Portal, including impacts on submitting claims, submitting prior authorizations, and checking member eligibility
  • Provider Enrollment Application (PEA)
  • Value-Based Purchasing Management System (VMS) Portal
  • Paper & fax document submissions
  • Provider Services & Member Services call centers
  • Value Added Network (VAN) Trading Partners
  • Prior authorizations for prescriptions and behavioral health services
  • Electronic Visit Verification (EVV)

You can also check the OMS Provider Resources webpage, in the first box of information called “Health PAS Online Portal,” for the most recent information about the upgrade.

For questions or clarifications, please contact Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. Please note, Provider Services does not have additional information beyond what is shared in this message and in the FAQ linked above.

entry.title: Expanding Affordable Housing in Maine — Governor of Maine — Newsroom Press Releases
entry.content:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

You know, we want every person at every stage of their life to be confident they can rent or buy a home that's the right size for their family and for their budget and be able to stay there as long as they want. No one should be afraid that a sudden rent increase will break their budget or that someone will buy the land right out from under them and raise rents.

When Hidden Circle Mobile Home Park in Jay went up for sale, that's exactly what the residents were afraid of: someone hiking up the rent and eventually pushing people out of their homes.

According to the 2024 data, nearly 10 percent of Maine people live in manufactured housing, including mobile home communities. Forty-five thousand people in Maine live in a mobile home park. Out-of-state companies have started buying up some of Maine's mobile home parks and then significantly raising rents, in some cases as high as 50 percent. 

And rent increases don't necessarily mean nicer parks either, no improvements necessarily. Corporations know that residents can't easily pick up their home and move it elsewhere, no matter how much the company neglects the park. As one resident in Jay said, "At one time, the park used to look nice. Now they've stopped that, and yet they have increased our rent. If this continues to have higher lot rent payments, then I'm not going to be able to live where I am."

The buying up of mobile home parks by out-of-state entities is a nationwide trend, but here in Maine, we're doing something about it. Last year, we enacted the "Right of First Refusal" law, which requires that residents of a mobile home park be given a chance to purchase their park if they can put together a matching offer when it's put up for sale. That measure strengthened our 2023 "Opportunity to Purchase" law, which required that residents of a mobile home park be allowed to present a competitive offer to buy their park if it's put up for sale.

Well, earlier this week, I visited Jay to celebrate the first residents to take advantage of our new "Right of First Refusal" law to purchase their park, instead of being left to the whims of an out-of-state buyer. Hidden Circle is now the 14th resident-owned manufactured home community in Maine. Resident-owned—isn't that great?

In addition to financing from the Genesis Fund and Maine Community Foundation, Hidden Circle Mobile Home Community was able to make the $1 million purchase to protect these 31 lots with $310,000 as well from our Mobile Home Park Preservation Fund.

My Administration and the Legislature dedicated $8 million in total in recent years to MaineHousing to create this Mobile Home Park Preservation Fund to assist residents in purchasing their own mobile home parks. With that funding, more than 900 homes are expected to be preserved across six parks from Brunswick to Bangor, Turner to Saco.

Last month, nation-leading laws to further protect mobile home park residents took effect in Maine, including laws to limit rent increases, laws to make it easier to expand mobile home parks, and laws creating a way for mobile homeowners to obtain a mortgage—and that could save them hundreds of dollars every month in housing costs.

I was proud to sign those bills into law earlier this year to protect residents in Jay and other towns across Maine from predatory, out-of-state companies. Now, the residents of Hidden Circle Park in Jay have control over how much rent to charge and how that money will be spent. They have control over their common infrastructure, and they can make improvements as they see fit.

Well, we still have a lot more work to do to protect Maine people and mobile home parks from being exploited by companies who simply want to use them to extract a profit, but I am proud of how we worked together with the Legislature to preserve this vital form of housing for people in Maine.

This is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

The Employment Situation in Maine - July 2026

August 21, 2026

Released: 10 a.m. Friday, August 21, 2026

Contact: Mark McInerney, (207) 620-0197

The Employment Situation in Maine - July 2026

The 3.1 unemployment rate was unchanged for the fourth consecutive month. Nonfarm wage and salary jobs have remained within a narrow range for 27 consecutive months.

Seasonally Adjusted Statewide Labor Force Estimates

The unemployment rate remained at 3.1 percent in July. Unemployment rates have remained within a narrow range between 3.1 and 3.3 percent for 23 consecutive months. Unemployment has been below four percent for 55 months, the longest duration on record. Maine's unemployment rate has been below the U.S. average for more than 18 years, and remains below the long-term average of 5.4 percent for the state since 1976. Unemployment averaged 4.2 percent for New England and 4.1 percent for the U.S. in the month.

The labor force participation rate averaged 59 percent in the last three months, modestly lower than the three months through April. The employment-to-population ratio was also modestly lower in the three months through July compared to the three months prior.

Seasonally Adjusted Statewide Nonfarm Jobs Estimates

Preliminary seasonally adjusted estimates indicate that in July, nonfarm wage and salary jobs were little changed from June. Most sectors exhibited little net job change over-the-month.

Job estimates have stayed within a narrow range near 660,000 for 27 consecutive months (estimates ranging less than one half of one percent higher or lower each month). Over the last year, a decrease in jobs in the professional and business services sector and smaller decreases in other sectors were mostly offset by increases that were also spread across several sectors.

These estimates are derived from two monthly surveys. The Current Population Survey collects information from households on labor force status, including labor force participation, employment, and unemployment. The Current Employment Statistics survey collects information from nonfarm employers by industry on the number of wage and salary jobs, hours worked, and wages paid to individuals on their payrolls. Both surveys are administered by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. Preliminary estimates from the two surveys sometimes diverge in direction or magnitude of change. Over extended periods they tend to be more aligned. The Current Population Survey of households was not conducted during the federal government shutdown that began in October 2025, no labor force estimates are available for that month.

Not Seasonally Adjusted County and Metro Area Labor Force Estimates

On a not seasonally adjusted basis the statewide unemployment rate was 3.0 percent. Rates were at least 0.3 percentage points higher than that in eight counties, at least 0.3 points lower than that in four, and close to the average in four. Rates were lowest in coastal counties and highest along the northern rim of the state.

Among the three metro areas, unemployment was below the statewide average in Portland-S. Portland, and close to the average in Bangor and Lewiston-Auburn.

Labor force estimates for substate areas, including unemployment rates, are not seasonally adjusted. Because of this, estimates for a certain month should be compared to the same month in other years and should not be compared to other months in the same or other years.

Not Seasonally Adjusted Statewide and Metro Area Hours and Earnings Estimates
